extracted.intended_audience: researchers, universities, small businesses, and contractors seeking DARPA funding or awards; proposal teams and contracting officers interacting with DARPA CMO
extracted.subtask_description: Official summary of the DARPA Contracts Management Office authority, the award vehicles it uses (contracts, grants/cooperative agreements, other transactions), and the governing policies and submission expectations for those vehicles. Useful for prospective proposers and organizations determining the appropriate solicitation or award mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMO authority and award vehicle types
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Contracts Management Office (CMO) has the authority to enter into and administer contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, and other transactions on behalf of DARPA. This includes: Broad Agency Announcements (BAAs); Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) topics; Small Business Technology Transfer Research (STTR) topics; Research Announcements (RAs) for grants or cooperative agreements; Requests for Proposals (RFPs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate DARPA award vehicle for your proposed work: respond to BAAs, SBIR/STTR topics, RAs for grants/cooperative agreements, or RFPs as applicable. Explore open opportunities via DARPA's opportunities list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement contract governance (FAR/DFARS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement contracts are governed by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and the DOD supplement (DFARS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such awards include standard FAR and DFARS clauses and are subject to the FAR cost accounting standards. Proposers and contractors must comply with FAR/DFARS requirements and applicable cost accounting rules when bidding on or performing under procurement contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants and cooperative agreements governance (2 C.F.R. 200 and DOD terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants and cooperative agreements with non-profit and educational institutions are subject to DOD Research and Development General Terms and Conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These awards are governed by the cost principles and requirements in 2 C.F.R. 200 and any subsequent DOD regulation and DARPA-specific terms and conditions. Prospective awardees should follow 2 C.F.R. 200 cost principles and DARPA’s stated terms for grants/cooperative agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and purpose of Other Transactions (OTs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Other Transactions' award vehicle enables work with organizations that do not often do business with the government but whose research could have DOD applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OTs may also be used with traditional defense contractors or universities. Consider OT as an option when partnering with nontraditional performers or when flexibility from traditional procurement/grant rules is desirable. See Acquisition Innovation Hub for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting of Justifications and Approvals (transparency requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: We post justifications and approvals for awards on the System for Award Management (sam.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting decisions that require written justifications/approvals will be made publicly available on SAM.gov in accordance with federal transparency requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolicited proposals policy (FAR Subpart 15.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsolicited proposals are subject to strict policies and procedures under FAR Subpart 15.6 – Unsolicited Proposals concerning submission, receipt, evaluation, and acceptance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA does not encourage submission of unsolicited proposals. If there is no suitable open solicitation, proposers should use the contact form to connect with CMO to determine whether their proposal is appropriate. Follow FAR 15.6 procedures if submitting an unsolicited proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available DARPA proposer resources and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of resources is provided to assist proposers (e.g., Proposer Communication Plan, Guide to BAAs and RAs, DI 20 | Soliciting, Evaluating, and Selecting Proposals, DI 70 | Contractor Relationships, Standard cost proposal spreadsheets, EEI milestones examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult DARPA-provided resources and templates (Acquisition Innovation Hub, proposer’s instructions, general terms and conditions, cost proposal spreadsheets, sample milestones) to align proposals with DARPA expectations and required formats. Use the RSS feed for Opportunities to track solicitations.
